extracted.intended_audience: Researchers who perform and report in vivo animal experiments; journal editors and peer reviewers assessing animal research reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting checklist for manuscripts describing in vivo animal experiments (ARRIVE guidelines 2.0). Intended to ensure manuscripts include minimum information for assessing reliability and to provide recommended contextual items as best practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; a core element authors must report to allow assessment of the reliability of findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — the basic minimum that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research. Without information on study design readers and reviewers cannot assess reliability. Each ARRIVE item on the website includes detailed explanations and examples of good reporting. See the Explanation and Elaboration (PLOS Biology doi:10.1371/journal.pbio.3000411).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; reporting required details about how sample size was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — the basic minimum that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research. Guidance on sample size includes minimisation of bias and statistical considerations; examples of good reporting are provided on the ARRIVE site and in the Explanation & Elaboration paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; report predefined inclusion/exclusion criteria and any exclusions during the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — necessary for readers/reviewers to judge whether the reported data are representative and unbiased. ARRIVE provides examples and explanatory text to help authors plan and report these elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; report whether and how allocation to experimental groups was randomized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — crucial to minimise selection bias. The ARRIVE materials include explanations for methods, reporting expectations, and example good practice from the literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; report whether experimenters and analysts were blinded to group allocation/outcomes where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — blinding reduces performance and detection biases. ARRIVE provides guidance and examples of reporting blinding or explaining why blinding was not possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; describe primary and secondary outcome measures and how they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — clear reporting of outcome measures is necessary to interpret results and appropriateness of analyses. ARRIVE includes examples and suggested reporting detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; describe statistical methods used, including software and how assumptions were checked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — statistical reporting enables assessment of analysis rigor and reproducibility. ARRIVE's Explanation & Elaboration provides detail on what to report (tests, assumptions, handling of data).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; report characteristics of animals used (species, strain, sex, age, weight, provenance, health status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — animal characteristics affect generalisability and reproducibility. ARRIVE provides examples of good reporting across taxa and study types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; provide sufficient procedural detail to allow replication, including timing, dosages, and equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — detailed procedures are needed for reproducibility. The ARRIVE site gives exemplar reports and advice on the level of detail required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Essential 10 items; report all results for each experiment, including summary statistics and effect sizes with confidence intervals where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Essential 10 — complete result reporting is necessary for interpretation and meta-analysis. ARRIVE recommends reporting summary measures, variability, and appropriate measures of effect and precision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; include key study features and findings in the abstract to aid indexing and reader appraisal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — complements the Essential 10 and provides important context; reporting these items represents best practice. ARRIVE provides examples of concise abstracts that include design, animal model, key methods, and main outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; provide scientific background and rationale for the study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — helps readers understand the study context and hypothesis. ARRIVE offers guidance and examples on framing background information appropriate to the animal model and objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; state specific objectives, hypotheses, or research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — clear objectives link study design and analyses to interpretation. ARRIVE includes examples of well-stated objectives and how to report pre-specified hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; report ethical approvals, licensing, and the ethical review process governing the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — reporting ethical oversight and compliance is best practice. ARRIVE provides examples of appropriate ethical statements and information to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; report housing, husbandry, and environmental conditions that could affect outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — contextual details (e.g., light/dark cycle, temperature, enrichment) influence reproducibility and animal welfare. ARRIVE provides examples and expected reporting granularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; describe welfare-related monitoring, interventions, and humane endpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — reporting care and monitoring practices is important for ethical transparency and data interpretation. ARRIVE gives examples across models and study types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; discuss the interpretation of results, limitations, and scientific implications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — authors should contextualise findings, acknowledge limitations, and avoid overstating conclusions. ARRIVE provides guidance on appropriate interpretation and reporting of limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; comment on the generalisability of findings and potential for translation to other systems or humans where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — authors should consider and report on external validity and translational relevance. ARRIVE supplies examples and advice on framing generalisability appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; report whether study protocols were registered or pre-specified and where they can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — protocol registration improves transparency and helps prevent selective reporting. ARRIVE encourages reporting registration details and provides examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; state whether and how the underlying data, code, and materials can be accessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — data access supports reproducibility and reuse. ARRIVE recommends including data availability statements and points to examples and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the ARRIVE Recommended Set items; declare conflicts of interest and funding sources that might influence the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended Set — transparent declarations of interests and funding are best practice. ARRIVE provides examples of appropriate declarations to include.
